pianoBasics.tapToHear: Tap any key to hear it.
pianoBasics.keyboardIntro: Keys repeat every 12: 7 white (natural notes) and 5 black (altered notes, sharp ♯ or flat ♭). Every black key has two names: C♯ is the same as D♭.
pianoBasics.findC: C is always just to the left of the group of 2 black keys.
pianoBasics.blackKeys: Black keys come in groups of 2 and 3; that pattern guides you across the whole keyboard.
pianoBasics.octavesIntro: An 88-key piano goes from A0 to C8. Each octave starts on C and is numbered: C1, C2… Middle C (C4, highlighted) sits in the middle of the piano and is the reference for placing your hands. Shown here from C1 to B7; the outermost keys complete the 88.
pianoBasics.middleCHint: Middle C = C4. Tap the keys to hear the octaves go up.
pianoBasics.fingersIntro: Each finger has a number on both hands, from thumb (1) to pinky (5). In the starting position, the left hand rests on C3–G3 (5-4-3-2-1) and the right hand on C4–G4 (1-2-3-4-5).
pianoBasics.tonesIntro: A half step (semitone) is the distance from one key to the very next, white or black. A whole step (tone) is two half steps. Tap each card to hear it.
pianoBasics.semitoneTitle: Half step without a black key
pianoBasics.semitone: E–F (and B–C) are half steps: there is no black key between them.
pianoBasics.semitoneBlack: C–C♯: from one key to the very next.
pianoBasics.tone: C–D: two half steps (skipping the black key in between).

scales.title: {root} {name}

desc.major: Bright and happy: the foundation of Western music. Also called the Ionian mode.
desc.minor: Melancholic and dark; the relative minor of the major scale. Also called the Aeolian mode.
desc.pentatonic-major: Five notes with no half steps: it almost always sounds right. Great for country, pop and melodic solos.
desc.pentatonic-minor: The go-to scale for improvising in rock, blues and pop. Five notes, easy to move around the neck.
desc.blues: The minor pentatonic plus the “blue note” (♭5), which gives it its signature sound.
desc.harmonic-minor: Minor with a raised 7th: sounds classical, Spanish or Middle Eastern. The V chord is major.
desc.melodic-minor: Minor with a raised 6th and 7th (ascending form). Widely used in jazz.
desc.dorian: Minor with a major 6th: less sad. Funk, jazz, rock (Santana, “Oye Como Va”).
desc.phrygian: Minor with a minor 2nd: a flamenco and metal sound.
desc.lydian: Major with a raised 4th: a dreamy sound, common in film scores.
desc.mixolydian: Major with a minor 7th: the scale of the dominant chord. Rock, blues and funk.
desc.locrian: The most unstable: diminished 2nd and 5th. Used over the half-diminished chord.

scales.formulaHint: W = whole step · H = half step · 1½ = step and a half

scales.positionsIntro: Practice the scale by zones: each position spans 4 frets, one finger per fret (1 = index … 4 = pinky; 0 = open string).
scales.chordsIntro: The chords built from its notes (stacked thirds). Tap one to see all its shapes.
